title: Compliance
description: Control status and audit evidence across regulatory frameworks. Not a certification — what the platform can evidence, and what it cannot yet.

framework.label: Framework
framework.selectHint: Pick a framework above to see its control gaps, the evidence behind each control, and what is still unmapped.

status.label: Status mix
status.byDesignHint: Design-ready means provided by the platform architecture — a design guarantee with no per-tenant telemetry. It is not the same as operational evidence.

groups.crosswalkHint: These are threat models, guidance and overlays the platform maps capabilities against to signal coverage. They are NOT conformance standards — no certification or conformance is claimed.
groups.inDevelopmentBanner: In development — not a final standard.
groups.designTowardBanner: Design-toward crosswalk — no conformance or certification is claimed.

posture.title: Compliance posture
posture.description: A per-framework status roll-up. Open a framework to inspect each control and the capabilities behind it.
posture.controlsDescription: Each control with its status and, expandable, the capabilities that evidence it.
posture.noCapabilities: No capability is mapped to this control yet.

class.operationalHint: Backed by live telemetry for this tenant.
class.architecturalHint: Provided by design and cited — not measured per tenant.

capabilityHint.resource_accounting: Operational compute/cost accounting only (EU AI Act Annex IV(2)(c)) — NOT dataset quality, energy consumption or carbon footprint, and not training-time figures.
capabilityHint.external_activity: Anthropic Compliance-API audit/eDiscovery evidence, counted separately — it is recorded activity evidence, NOT a security alert.
capabilityHint.supplier_gpai_posture: A supplier's GPAI posture is a CLAIM, not evidence, unless it has been operator-verified. Self-reported, unverified postures do not count as evidence.

gaps.title: What to fix
gaps.description: Controls that are not yet satisfied, ordered by status. Each row lists the capabilities to turn on to close the gap.
gaps.empty: No open gaps for this framework.
gaps.emptyHint: A gap is a control with no operational evidence. This framework has none open: every mapped control is satisfied or design-ready.
gaps.noMissing: No specific capability identified — review the criterion.

evidence.portableHint: Stored evidence packages remain available for JSON and CSV export.
evidence.title: Audit evidence
evidence.description: Sealed evidence packages with a tamper-evidence integrity check and a ledger anchor. A package is control status plus proof of integrity — never a certificate.
evidence.emptyHint: Seal a package to anchor the current control status to the audit ledger.

dialog.title: Seal evidence package
dialog.description: Anchor the current control status for this framework to the audit ledger. This read is privileged and recorded.

export.label: Export
export.oscalHint: OSCAL finding status is a 2-value enum (satisfied / not-satisfied). A design-ready control is exported as not-satisfied with the real status in its reason — never relabelled as satisfied.
export.oscalSectionDescription: The honest mapping of each control onto the OSCAL 2-value status, with the real product status preserved alongside.

risk.title: Agent risk register
risk.description: EU AI Act risk tier per agent, cross-mapped to NIST AI RMF functions. The heuristic never assigns the unacceptable tier — it appears only after human review.
risk.emptyHint: Agents are listed here with the risk tier their classification gives them. Classify an agent to see it appear.

declaration.declared: Declarations do not prove execution or safe behavior.
declaration.none_declared: No active declaration found. Behavior is unknown.
declaration.partial: Declaration coverage is partial. Behavior is unknown.
declaration.unavailable: Declaration source unavailable. Behavior is unknown.

risk.unacceptableNote: The unacceptable tier is only ever set by a human reviewer — the heuristic never assigns it.

dialog.title: Review risk classification
dialog.description: Approve the suggested tier or override it. Overriding to unacceptable is a deliberate human decision.

residency.title: Data residency
residency.description: Attested regions with their perimeter, encryption at rest, and any observed egress violations.
residency.emptyHint: Regions attested for this tenant appear here with the evidence behind them. No region has been attested yet.

retention.title: Retention schedules
retention.description: Per-class disposal schedules, the sweeps that run them, and the sealed certificate each sweep leaves behind. A schedule documents intent; only an approved purge destroys anything.
retention.noAccess: You do not have access to retention schedules
retention.noAccessHint: Retention schedules decide how long each class of record is kept. Ask an administrator for the retention read permission.
retention.gateHint: A schedule is a document until a human approves its purge. Saving one never deletes data; a sweep does.
retention.notRunning: Retention is not running: this database cannot list every tenant.
retention.noClasses: The engine returned no data classes
retention.noClassesHint: The class registry is fixed in the engine, so an empty list does not mean an empty tenant — it means this response could not be read as the registry. Reload, and report it if it persists.
retention.rowPurging: Rows older than {{days}} days are deleted on every sweep.
retention.rowPurgingClamped: Rows older than {{days}} days are deleted on every sweep — the schedule says {{scheduled}}, but the {{basis}} floor holds the sweep back.
retention.rowRetaining: Retained for {{days}} days. This schedule deletes nothing.
retention.rowUnscheduled: No schedule: nothing here is disposed of on a timetable.
retention.rowUnscheduledAdvised: No schedule: nothing here is disposed of on a timetable. Advisory guidance: {{days}} days.
retention.disclosure: Gone everywhere after {{days}} days — the honest disclosure window, the provider’s own floor included.
retention.disclosureUnknown: The provider retention floor is unknown, so no “gone everywhere after” window can be stated for this class.
retention.regulatoryFloor: Regulatory floor: {{days}} days ({{basis}}, {{mode}} mode). Nothing younger is deleted.
retention.author: Add schedule

dialog.title: Schedule for {{class}}
dialog.description: Document how long this class is kept, and what happens at the end of that window.
dialog.dispositionHint: Retain documents the window. Purge deletes rows past it, and needs human approval before it comes into force.
dialog.notPurgeableHint: This class cannot be purged on a timetable, so only Retain is offered. The documented schedule is still evidence.
dialog.basisHint: The regulation, contract or policy this window comes from. It travels into the approval request.
dialog.enabledHint: Turn it off to keep the document without letting a sweep act on it.
dialog.willDestroy: This arms deletion of {{class}} rows older than {{days}} days on every sweep, until you turn it off.
dialog.armDescription: This authorises repeated destruction, not one deletion.
dialog.armScope: Every sweep will DELETE rows of {{class}} older than {{days}} days. Deletion is permanent and cannot be undone.
dialog.armApproval: The purge comes into force only once a human approves it. Until then the schedule is saved with the purge switched off.
dialog.pendingTitle: Approval requested — the purge is OFF
dialog.pendingDescription: The engine opened an approval instead of arming the schedule.
dialog.pendingDisabled: The schedule for {{class}} was saved, but the purge is NOT in force: no sweep will act on it until a human approves it.
dialog.savedPurging: Schedule saved, and the purge is in force
dialog.savedRetaining: Schedule saved. Nothing is deleted by it.
dialog.saveUnconfirmed: The engine accepted the request but did not return the schedule, so it cannot be confirmed
dialog.noGate: No approval gate is wired, so arming a purge is denied. The purge was not armed.
dialog.approvalExpired: The approval expired. Save again to request a new one.
dialog.underFloor: The window is shorter than the regulatory floor for this class
dialog.removed: Schedule removed. Nothing is scheduled for this class.
dialog.sealed: This schedule is sealed as evidence and cannot be removed
dialog.removeDescription: Removing a schedule stops any disposal it authorised. No data is deleted by this.
dialog.removeScope: {{class}} keeps its data. It simply stops being disposed of on a timetable.

sweep.title: Run the retention sweep now
sweep.description: This deletes data. It runs the same pass the engine runs on its own schedule, attributed to you.
sweep.noneArmed: No schedule currently authorises destruction, so this sweep will delete nothing.
sweep.scopeIntro: This sweep will DELETE rows under the schedules in force ({{count}}):
sweep.scopeItemClamped: rows older than {{days}} days — the {{basis}} floor, not the {{scheduled}}-day schedule
sweep.holdsWin: A legal hold always beats a purge: a held class is skipped whole, and held rows are preserved.
sweep.unknownTitle: The schedules could not be read
sweep.unknownDescription: A sweep is not offered while its scope is unknown.
sweep.unknownScope: Without the schedules there is no way to tell you what this sweep would delete — and "nothing" would be a guess, not an answer. Read them again first.
sweep.failedPartial: The sweep failed part-way — rows deleted before it stopped are already gone

result.title: Last sweep
result.truncated: The sweep did NOT finish: it reached the per-class scan limit. Run it again to continue.
result.heldBack: Classes stopped entirely by a legal hold: {{count}}. Nothing in them was deleted.
result.complete: The sweep completed across every schedule in force.
result.totals: {{examined}} rows examined · {{purged}} deleted · {{excluded}} preserved under a legal hold.
result.noClasses: No schedule was in force, so nothing was examined.

runs.title: Destruction certificates
runs.description: One sealed, append-only certificate per class per sweep with activity, anchored in the audit ledger. This is the record an auditor asks for.
runs.emptyHint: A sweep seals one only for a class that examined rows or was stopped by a hold; a routine empty pass leaves no record.

holds.title: Legal holds
holds.description: Preservation orders that veto every destruction path, including GDPR erasure.
holds.noAccess: You do not have permission to read legal holds.
holds.noAccessHint: A legal hold freezes data from deletion while a matter is open. Ask an administrator for the legal-hold read permission.
holds.emptyHint: A hold preserves data against every deletion path until it is released under dual control.
holds.asymmetryHint: Placing a hold takes effect immediately — the duty to preserve admits no waiting. Releasing one requires two distinct approving user accounts and has no emergency override.
holds.custodyDescription: Append-only custody events, each anchored to the audit ledger head at the moment it was sealed.
holds.custodyEmptyHint: Each time a custodian is added, notified or released it is recorded here. This hold has no custody events yet.

dialog.createDescription: The hold takes effect immediately and blocks every destruction path that matches its scope.
dialog.matterHint: The case or matter this preservation order belongs to. Rejected if over-length — never truncated, because a shortened reference is a different identity.
dialog.title: Title
dialog.scopeHint: What the hold matches. Tenant covers everything; data class covers one registered class; subject covers one exact kind and reference.
dialog.tenantWarning: A tenant-scope hold blocks every deletion for this tenant, including scheduled retention sweeps.
dialog.dataClassHint: Picked from the registry: the engine rejects a class that is not registered exactly.
dialog.reasonHint: Recorded verbatim in the chain of custody.
dialog.notHeld: Nothing currently preserves this. The hold you are about to place would be the first.
dialog.created: Legal hold placed — preservation is active.
dialog.releaseDescription: Releasing lifts preservation. Data this hold protected becomes eligible for deletion again.
dialog.releaseScope: This hold currently {{scope}}. Releasing it removes that protection.
dialog.dualControl: This requires two distinct approving user accounts. There is no break-glass path.
dialog.pendingDescription: The release was requested and recorded in the chain of custody.
dialog.stillActive: The hold is STILL ACTIVE. Nothing has been released — preservation stays in force until two distinct user accounts approve. The engine enforces distinct ACCOUNTS; it cannot prove that two accounts are two different people.
dialog.releaseUnconfirmed: The release request was accepted, but the hold does not report itself as released — check the holds list before assuming preservation was lifted.
dialog.createUnconfirmed: The request was accepted, but the hold is not confirmed as placed — check the holds list before relying on preservation.
dialog.releaseIncompleteUnknown: The release did NOT complete and the hold is STILL ACTIVE. The control plane gave a reason this console does not recognise — check the hold before assuming anything.

erasure.title: Right to erasure & data-subject requests
erasure.description: Registered erasure requests, their dual-control execution and the verifiable receipt each one seals.
erasure.noAccess: You do not have permission to read erasure requests.
erasure.noAccessHint: Erasure and subject-access requests are tracked here with their legal deadlines. Ask an administrator for the erasure read permission.
erasure.subject: Subject
erasure.emptyHint: Registering a request is safe: it mints the subject key and records the request. Nothing is destroyed until you execute it.
erasure.irreversibleHint: Executing an erasure is irreversible. It destroys the subject's key, which permanently renders every token for them unintelligible.
erasure.retained: What is deliberately retained, and why
erasure.providerFloor: The model provider retains input and output for {{days}} days regardless of this erasure ({{source}}). Deleting our copy does not delete theirs.
erasure.receiptDescription: The sealed, ledger-anchored proof of an executed erasure.
erasure.receiptDisclaimer: This receipt evidences the erasure the control plane performed over its own stores. It is not legal advice and does not certify compliance.
erasure.lookupDescription: The per-subject answer to an Article 15 or 17 request.

dialog.registerDescription: This records the request and mints the subject key. It destroys nothing.
dialog.registerSafe: Registering is not destructive. The erasure only runs when you execute it, and only after both gates clear.
dialog.caseHint: Your DSAR case identifier. Rejected if over-length, never truncated.
dialog.aliasesHint: Comma-separated additional identifiers for the same person.
dialog.executeDescription: This runs the governed erasure across every store, then destroys the subject key.
dialog.irreversible: IRREVERSIBLE. Once the subject key is destroyed, every token referencing this person becomes permanently unintelligible. There is no undo and no restore.
dialog.twoGates: Two independent gates must clear first: no legal hold may cover this subject, and two distinct user accounts must approve. Neither can be skipped. The engine enforces distinct ACCOUNTS; it cannot prove that two accounts are two different people.
dialog.pendingDescription: The execution was requested and recorded in the chain of custody.
dialog.nothingErasedYet: NOTHING HAS BEEN ERASED. The request is waiting for two distinct user accounts to approve it.
dialog.blockedExplain: A legal hold covers this subject. Preservation wins over erasure: the hold must be released under dual control before this erasure can proceed.
dialog.executedWithGaps: Erasure executed WITH GAPS — the receipt records what could not be completed.
dialog.providerPending: PARTIALLY ERASED. Local data and the account leg ran, but the model provider still has deletions outstanding. The subject key has NOT been shredded and no receipt is sealed — re-execute once the provider approvals are granted.
dialog.incompleteUnknown: The erasure did NOT complete. The engine reported an outcome this console does not recognise — check the request status before assuming anything was destroyed.
dialog.coordinatorTitle: Blocked by the RTBF readiness check
dialog.coordinatorExplain: The Business RTBF coordinator refused to proceed. This is NOT a legal hold: fix the blockers below, then execute again.
dialog.holdsPayloadIncomplete: The engine reported a legal hold but the hold list came back incomplete. Check the holds screen before concluding what is preserved.
dialog.executedUnconfirmed: Erasure ran, but its final status could not be confirmed — open the request and read the receipt before treating it as finished.
dialog.refusedTitle: The control plane refused this erasure
dialog.registerUnconfirmed: The request was accepted, but it is not confirmed as registered — check the erasure list before relying on it.

erasure.noCustody: No custody events recorded for this request.
erasure.unanchored: NOT anchored to the ledger — recorded, not provable

calendar.title: Regulatory calendar
calendar.description: Dated regulatory milestones, each with its primary source and the date it was verified.
calendar.notInForceHint: Provisional agreements, texts adopted pending publication and in-development mappings are NOT in-force law. They are shown with their status so they are never read as obligations.
calendar.emptyHint: Regulatory milestones for the selected framework appear here with their due dates. Select another framework to see its calendar.
calendar.watchlistDescription: Tracked rulemakings, draft standards and pilots that have no date to cite yet.
calendar.watchlistEmptyHint: Milestones you follow appear here, so the nearest deadline is always on screen. Add one from the calendar above.

risk.title: No compliance risk classifications yet
risk.description: A caller must submit an agent to the compliance risk API; its observed signals and suggested EU AI Act tier are then recorded here.

claudeFiles.title: Provider file store
claudeFiles.noAccess: You do not have access to the file store inventory.
claudeFiles.noAccessHint: This tab inventories the files the store holds for governed sessions. Ask an administrator for the file-store read permission.

unwired.title: Erasure seam not configured
unwired.body: This is NOT "no files": the engine cannot enumerate or erase the store until an operator wires the connector. Nothing here has been checked.

empty.title: No files enumerated
empty.body: The seam is wired and the store reports no files for this tenant.

confirm.title: Erase this file?
confirm.body: A governed point delete. It may be refused by a legal hold, or require an approval before it takes effect — the result names which.

claudeFiles.reasonHint: Optional. Recorded in the audit ledger with the deletion.
claudeFiles.eraseFailed: The erase request could not be sent.

capabilities.title: Capability catalog
capabilities.description: What the platform can evidence right now for this tenant. Control status and evidence — never certification.

count.label: Rows
count.notCountedHint: Architectural capability: it rests on the design documents, so there are no rows to count. This is not a count of zero.

capabilities.emptyHint: The platform capabilities a framework can be evidenced against are listed here. The catalog returned none for this deployment.
capabilities.error: The capability catalog could not be read.

hipaa.title: HIPAA technical safeguards
hipaa.forbidden: You do not have permission to read compliance frameworks.
hipaa.forbiddenHint: This report maps HIPAA §164.312 to the controls the platform can evidence. Ask an administrator for the framework read permission.
hipaa.unreadable: The gap report could not be read.
hipaa.noControlsHint: The report lists each technical safeguard with the evidence behind it. The framework returned no controls for this deployment.
hipaa.byDesignNote: "By design only" means every mapped capability is present as a cited platform guarantee, not as live telemetry. The engine counts these as not fully backed.
